summary: Shannon County lookout whose survey station the site marks as removed. A 1939 survey describes a 110-foot steel tower, which conflicts with a CCC pine-pole build credit.

facts.design: Steel structure with an enclosed observation platform (1939 survey); a CCC pine-pole project is also credited
facts.status_note: Survey station marked removed on the site. No source describes what remains at the site today.

events.note: Coast and Geodetic Survey described the tower as a 110-foot steel structure with an enclosed observation platform
Rolla Herald item, quoted on the site, reports a fatal crash that killed the wife of a Forest Service towerman stationed near Bunker

notes_for_editor: One source: the Forest Lookouts page, which quotes a 1939 Coast and Geodetic Survey station description, a 1949 Rolla Herald item and a CCC build credit. The originals were not reached. The pine-pole credit and the 1939 steel-tower description conflict; the story says so and does not resolve it. The site gives no build year and no removal date, so there is no dated build or removal event. The 110 ft figure is not tied to the cab floor, so no height_m. Access and current condition are unknown. The Marcoot Fire Lookout (Reynolds County, Bunker address, Living New Deal) is a different tower and was not used. The 'Removed' label sits above the NGS survey-station block, so the story attributes removal to the survey station, not the tower.
